Quadro360.notes: None of the eleven inputs or four outputs is named in configInput or configOutput, so Rack's own tooltips are blank on all of them. The eight signal inputs are placed on the panel at angles that run the opposite way round from the angles the DSP gives them (widget loop at src/Quadro360.cpp:132-137 uses (2-i)*pi/4, process at line 82-83 uses i*0.785), so the drawn ring and the computed ring rotate in opposite directions; nothing on screen shows this. The constructor fills a 32769-float sqrts table but writes only sqrts[0], and the table is never read. Each output's gain is (128 - distance)/128, which is about 0.29 with both radius knobs at 100, and goes negative once the distance passes 128, which is reachable with the radius CVs.

PowVCO.notes: None of the six inputs or the output is named in configInput or configOutput, so Rack's tooltips are blank on all of them. RESET is tested as a level, not an edge, and it zeroes every one of the 16 channel phases at once even in polyphonic use. The module has two separate code paths: with V/OCT patched it runs a per-channel loop, and with V/OCT unpatched it runs a single-voice path. In the single-voice path the envelope's end-of-run setVoltage(0) at line 163 is overwritten by the unconditional setVoltage at line 178, so the output there holds the last computed sample instead of being forced to zero; with the default POW4 that value is 0V anyway, but with a negative POW4 and CLIP up it rests at 10V. In the polyphonic path the zero stands. The POW jacks add to their knobs with no clamp on the sum, so exponents outside -10 to +10 are reachable.

ColoredGlass.notes: None of the 22 inputs is named in configInput, so Rack's tooltips are blank on all of them. Particles[], ParticlesCopy[], Settings and colorshift are file-scope globals (src/ColoredGlass.cpp:46-78), not members, so every instance in a patch writes the same state; the last module's process() of each frame decides what all of them draw. The randomness jacks on EDGES and STROKE add a whole unit per volt while their knobs run only 0 to 1, whereas the other randomness jacks add a tenth per volt; the scalings are at src/ColoredGlass.cpp:168-188. RESET is a level test on the sum of the button and the jack, so a held gate above 0V restores the starting particles on every frame. The RED, GREEN and BLUE results are cast to an unsigned byte by nvgRGBA, so negative settings wrap; the factory default for RED is -9. There are no outputs.

ScaleMerger.notes: None of the 32 inputs or the output is named in configInput or configOutput, so Rack's tooltips are blank on all of them. scales[] holds 43 rows but scaleNames[] is written with a missing comma between "UKRAINIAN DORIAN" and "TURKISH" (src/ScaleMerger.cpp:64), so the two run together as one name and the array supplies only 42 of its 43 entries: the 42nd scale shows as UKRAINIAN DORIANTURKISH and the 43rd, the top of the SCALE knob, has a null name that the display's sprintf prints as (null). Quantising compares the fractional part of the input against each pitch's fractional position as integers scaled by 10000 (normalize(), line 209), with no wrap, so the distance from a pitch near the top of the octave to C is measured the long way round and the result never rounds up into the next octave. probs2 is computed twice, once through getProb and once by a direct expression at line 384, which gives the same answer. The unique-pitch PROBABILITY knobs multiply only pitches that one scale has and the other does not; shared pitches are never scaled. The per-channel loop at line 413 returns from process() rather than continuing when a channel has no trigger, so later channels are not written that sample; their jack voltages persist, which is the intended result anyway.

Math.notes: No port here is named in configInput or configOutput, so Rack's tooltips are blank on all 24 inputs and 15 outputs. Every cell is guarded by isConnected on both inputs and on its own output, so an unpatched output jack means the arithmetic is skipped and the jack keeps its last written value rather than falling to zero. There are no parameters at all. Nothing is clamped: a division by zero writes an infinity, and std::log of a negative voltage writes a not-a-number, either of which propagates into anything patched downstream. The B input is read with getVoltage(c) rather than getPolyVoltage(c), so it is not spread across channels. No family is given to any jack, because these carry whatever is patched into them.

CellularAuto.notes: None of the twelve inputs or the three outputs is named in configInput or configOutput, so Rack's tooltips are blank on all of them. Input 4 (ROTATE_INPUT) and parameter 10 (ROTATE_PARAM) are declared in the enums and given no widget, and ROTATE_PARAM has no configParam either, so neither can be reached or clicked; the jacks around them are not renumbered. The panel prints LEFT and TOP where configParam names the parameters X and Y. EOS tests Positions[c] == 0 (src/CellularAuto.cpp:354), but every channel above the first restarts at c * cells rather than 0, so EOS fires only on channel 0 however many channels the clock carries. RULE is clamped below at 0 and not above, and the rule byte is applied with a bitwise and against 1 << index, so anything above 255 acts as its remainder. Each ITER pass runs a full 256 rows carrying on from the last, so the grid kept is the last 256 generations. The four button inputs are summed with their buttons before a SchmittTrigger, so a steady voltage above 1V holds the trigger high and blocks further presses of the button beside it.
